preTest.title: Pre-study knowledge check
preTest.description: Answer these questions on your own before your group begins. This is not graded; it measures what you already know about collaborative learning and AI support.

questions.text: Which description best fits collaborative learning?
options: Each member completes a separate part and the parts are joined at the end
Members build a shared understanding together and are jointly responsible for the result
The strongest member does the task while the others watch and learn
Members compete to produce the best individual answer

questions.text: A group task has "positive interdependence" when:
options: Members can finish the task without talking to each other
One member is responsible for checking everyone else's work
The group is graded only on the speed of completion
The group can only succeed if every member contributes and members rely on each other

questions.text: Why is individual accountability important in group work?
options: It prevents members from relying on others and makes sure everyone learns
It lets the teacher identify the group leader
It allows members to work without discussing ideas
It makes group grades unnecessary
Giving students the complete solution so they can study it
Testing students before teaching them a topic
Giving temporary support that helps learners do what they cannot yet do alone
Dividing a class into groups of similar ability

questions.text: A group has written an answer that includes some correct ideas but also contains gaps in its explanation. The members want to improve their answer without having AI rewrite it. Which type of support would be most appropriate?
options: A brief explanation of the main concept to strengthen their understanding.
Feedback identifying weaknesses in their current answer and areas that need further reasoning.
An example of a similar problem showing how a strong answer could be developed.
A detailed explanation of how the problem should be solved, without providing the final answer.

questions.text: A group is working on a difficult problem. Members are exploring different approaches, testing ideas, and gradually making progress, although they have not reached an answer. What should determine whether AI assistance is needed?
options: Whether the group has spent more time than expected on the problem.
Whether the group has identified a possible solution but has not yet agreed on it.
Whether the difficulty is preventing further progress rather than encouraging useful exploration.
Whether the group could complete the task more quickly by receiving additional guidance.

questions.text: During a collaborative activity, all members contribute to the discussion, but some send significantly fewer messages than others. Which observation would provide the strongest evidence of meaningful collaboration?
options: Each member contributes approximately the same amount of written content to the final answer.
Members distribute tasks according to their knowledge and complete their assigned responsibilities.
Members have similar opportunities to express their opinions during the discussion.
Members consider, question, and build upon one another's ideas when developing their answer.

questions.text: A group receives an AI-generated explanation that seems convincing but differs from information the members previously discussed. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Request a second AI explanation and compare the two responses before selecting the most convincing one.
Examine the AI's reasoning against the available evidence and decide whether its suggestions are justified.
Incorporate the AI's explanation while noting that some parts may require further verification.
Compare the AI explanation with the group's original answer and retain whichever provides more detailed reasoning.

openQuestions.text:
A group is stuck repeating the same arguments without progress. One member suggests asking AI for the full answer.

What should AI do, who should receive the support, and how can the group remain responsible for the solution?

postTest.title: Post-study knowledge check
postTest.description: Answer these questions on your own after completing all scenarios. This is not graded; it measures what you learned during the activity.

options: Each member writes one section at home and one member pastes them together
One member writes the answer and the others agree without comment
Members discuss ideas, question each other and agree on one answer they all understand
Members each submit their own answer and the best one is chosen

questions.text: Which task design creates the strongest positive interdependence?
options: Each member holds different information that the group needs to combine to solve the problem
Each member solves the whole problem alone and the answers are averaged
One member solves the problem and explains it to the others
Members choose whether to take part

questions.text: Which practice best supports individual accountability in a group?
options: Giving only one shared grade with no other checks
Letting the group leader report on behalf of everyone
Allowing members to stay silent if the group finishes on time
Asking each member to explain the group's answer or rate their own contribution

questions.text: According to scaffolding theory, how much help should a learner receive?
options: As much as possible, so mistakes are avoided
The least help needed to make progress, reduced as the learner improves
No help, because struggling is always beneficial
The same amount of help for every learner

questions.text: A group has drafted its recommendation, but the draft does not explain why the other options were rejected. The members want help improving that draft rather than receiving a new answer. Which support is most appropriate?
options: A full explanation of the preferred recommendation, without writing the group's final paragraph.
An example from another subject showing how alternatives can be compared.
Feedback on the draft that identifies the missing justification and asks the group to supply it.
A brief definition of every option so the group can begin the discussion again.

questions.text: A group is uncertain, but its members are still proposing reasons, challenging them and revising their idea. Which judgement best decides whether they should ask the AI for help?
options: They should ask only if the uncertainty has stopped them from making any further progress.
They should ask because uncertainty shows that their current ideas are not good enough.
They should ask whenever the scenario takes longer than the suggested discussion time.
They should ask so that the AI can choose the strongest idea they have already proposed.

questions.text: Two members send many chat messages while the third sends fewer. Which result best shows that the group still collaborated meaningfully?
options: The three members finish with almost equal shares of the final text.
The third member's suggestion is discussed, questioned and used to change the group's answer.
The group divides the remaining writing so each member adds the same number of sentences.
Every member receives an equal opportunity to send a message before submission.

questions.text: The AI gives a clear explanation, but it contradicts an example the group discussed earlier. What should the group do next?
options: Accept the AI explanation because it is clearer than the group's example.
Ask the AI to explain the same point again in more detail before deciding.
Keep both ideas in the answer so that neither the AI nor the group is rejected.
Check the AI explanation against the example and the other available evidence before deciding what to keep.

openQuestions.text:
A group is stuck repeating the same arguments without progress. One member suggests asking AI for the full answer.

What should AI do, who should receive the support, and how can the group remain responsible for the solution?
